title: Compute brief - 6 November 2026
description: Microsoft is tightening oversight of Nebius, IREN and Nscale while Google still writes a $17 billion Wyoming campus cheque, and Lambda just raised on-demand list prices across its 8x stack. Wire: Google Wyoming $17B / 702 MW Bloom+CCS, Amazon's Comanche Peak nuclear campus, TeraWulf's Anthropic Kentucky EPC. Tape: 66 confirms, 4 ticks (all Lambda), 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The offtaker is cutting optionality. The list price just moved.
lede: A day after the election selloff priced regulatory risk into neoclouds, the stack repriced delivery and list rates. Bloomberg via Reuters said Microsoft is tightening oversight of projects at Nebius, IREN and Nscale and debating new neocloud contracts as it prioritises owned sites; IREN's Q1 put its >$4 billion ARR target into January 2027 after a Microsoft-requested network redesign at Childress. Hyperscalers are still converting land into campuses they control: Google posted a $17 billion first Wyoming data centre with a 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell CCS plant, Amazon confirmed a Somervell County campus as a direct Comanche Peak nuclear offtaker, and TeraWulf locked Fluor EPC plus a Google credit backstop for Anthropic's ~401 MW Justified lease in Kentucky. On the public tape, Lambda raised 8x on-demand prints overnight — B200 $6.69 to $7.69, H100 $3.99 to $4.59, A100-80GB $2.79 to $3.19, GH200 $2.29 to $2.59 — while CoreWeave H100 held $6.16 and Crusoe's 1 December column stayed scheduled, not live. Tape: 66 confirms, 4 ticks, 0 NEW.
